message:
Plain words: the raised rear pour clears the bin lip and stays upright on flat ground if trips stay light. The Skid-Steer Safety for Farm and Landscape (E47) rule I take is that lifting a load transfers weight and raises the centre of gravity, meaning centre of gravity (CG, meaning balance point of the machine), so a raised heavy load can tip the machine, and the dump clearance simulation (E51) puts the hopper pivot at 0.550 m over a 0.400 m bin lip for 0.150 m clearance shown in the side view rear dump sketch (E53). Stabilising moment is about 81.0 N m against about 47.8 N m overturning with 15.0 kg soil plus 4.50 kg steel for a safety factor of 1.69, everyday scale like a loaded wheelbarrow held down by a person, much smaller than the earlier 4.67 in the stowed envelope sum, ground pressure, tip-over and stopping check (E23), so Excavation and Regolith Handling Lead please keep trips to 15.0 kg and dump only on level ground.

Plain words: a spinning cross-drum loosens soil with little push, which fits a light skid chassis. The Single Drum Trench Cutters | Transverse Cutter | Trenching Attachment (E45) finding I take is that transverse cutters concentrate all power into a single drum for high productivity in tough ground, and the Transverse Drum (E46) finding I take is that transverse drums deliver high-precision cutting power for demanding excavation, so the transverse milling drum loosener (C31) milling 300 mm wide by 50 mm deep and throwing soil back maps rotary tiller cutting to this low-traction robot. Forward draft stays well below the 32.9 N cut load from the BP-1 shallow scraper cut force estimate (E9) against 294 N traction from the stowed envelope sum, ground pressure, tip-over and stopping check (E23), everyday scale about 3 kg push against a 60 kg machine, so traction margin stays comfortable.

Plain words: Power Structure and Integration Lead is right that the frame is too bendy, and my arms still stow in the box. I confirm the Aluminum square tubing strength (E38) rule that 6061-T6, meaning aluminium alloy 6061 in T6 temper, allows about 15,000 psi working stress, where psi means pounds per square inch, and the Microsoft Word - FTOF Panel 1B Frame Analysis.docx (E50) rule I take is that a frame passes only when stresses stay below allowable and deflections stay acceptable, so stiffness not strength decides here: single-rail sag 72.9 mm from the cantilever deflection estimate frame rail (E43) shared over two rails is still 36.5 mm from the twin rail sag share check (E52), a hand width not millimetre wobble. Stowed size is 0.900 m long by 0.420 m track in the dump clearance simulation (E51) inside the 1.00 m by 0.500 m by 0.500 m limit, deploying to 1.05 m long by 0.680 m track with 0.110 m wheel radius and 0.025 m rotation gap. Not ready, because the frame needs larger second moment of area, meaning shape stiffness designated I, or truss bracing before build.
